question: In crush syndrome, renal failure results from direct mechanical compression of the kidneys rather than from myoglobin released by the compressed muscle.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Renal failure in crush syndrome is caused by myoglobinuria. Crushed muscle releases myoglobin; this brown-coloured molecule is filtered by the glomerulus, precipitates in distal tubules (especially in acidic urine), and causes tubular obstruction and ischaemia. This is distinct from any direct mechanical injury to the kidney.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Crush syndrome (traumatic rhabdomyolysis) causes renal failure through myoglobinuria, not direct kidney compression. Prolonged compression releases myoglobin from necrotic muscle; myoglobin precipitates in renal tubules, causing tubular obstruction and ischaemic acute tubular necrosis.
